Tests for {@link InternationalFixedChronology} and {@link InternationalFixedDate}.

The International Fixed Calendar (IFC) divides the year into 13 months of exactly 28 days each (4 weeks × 7 days), so every month starts on a Sunday. Two extra days are outside the regular week structure and carry day-of-week value 0:

  • Year Day – month 13, day 29; appended at the end of every year.
  • Leap Day – month 6, day 29; inserted after month 6 only in leap years.
Leap years follow the same rule as the ISO/Gregorian calendar: a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4, except century years which are only leap years when also divisible by 400 (e.g. 1900 is not a leap year; 2000 is).

IFC date {@code 0001-01-01} is aligned with ISO {@code 0001-01-01}.

Verifies {@code minus()} by reusing {@code data_plus}: each row in that dataset has the form {@code (input, amount, unit, expected)}. Subtracting {@code amount} from {@code expected} must recover {@code input}, so the parameters here are intentionally in reversed order — {@code (expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDom)} first, then {@code (year, month, dom)}.

Same parameter-reversal convention as {@link #test_minus_TemporalUnit}: reuses {@code data_minus_leap_and_year_day} where each row already encodes {@code (input, amount, unit, expected)} for minus — no extra reversal needed here.
